dedupe_keys.name: blond building level office environment dataset

description: BLOND is a dataset of continuous high-frequency electricity measurements from a typical office environment, built for research on non-intrusive load monitoring, which infers appliance use from aggregate building meters. It was produced by Thomas Kriechbaumer and Hans-Arno Jacobsen at the Technical University of Munich and published on the mediaTUM repository in August 2017, with a paper in Scientific Data (2018). It gives voltage and current for aggregated circuits in a three-phase grid together with fully labelled ground truth from 53 individual appliances of 17 classes; BLOND-50 covers 213 days of uninterrupted measurements at 50,000 samples per second for the aggregate and 6,400 per appliance, and BLOND-250 is a higher-rate variant. Data production ended on 30 June 2017. Access: download through the web, FTP or rsync; the whole set is about 38.7 TB in 945,919 HDF5 files. Licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0; free. Caveats: one office building in Germany, and the volume makes full download impractical for most users. Simulation uses are appliance-level load models for office buildings, training disaggregation methods, and realistic plug-load inputs for building digital twins. Related records: the LBNL Building 59 dataset and the GECAD smart building datasets.
